extra.message: User-controlled filterValue (from GET ?filterValue in src/app/api/reports/route.ts) is concatenated directly into a raw SQL string interpolated with '%...%' and executed via prisma.$queryRawUnsafe(query). This allows SQL injection.

sortField is used as the ORDER BY column with a `??` fallback: if it is not in ROSTER_SORT_COLUMNS, the raw user-supplied value is interpolated into the ORDER BY clause and executed via $queryRawUnsafe. User-controlled sortField (GET ?sortField) allows SQL injection.

convertDocumentForRelease builds a shell command with exec() using template-string interpolation of user-controlled outputFormat (from the request body in src/app/api/documents/convert/route.ts). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. `; rm -rf ...`) to execute arbitrary OS commands.

renderDocumentFromTemplate joins the attacker-controlled templateName (read from the `letterheadTemplate` cookie in src/app/api/documents/[id]/letterhead/route.ts) directly into a filesystem path without any containment check (unlike renderVisitSummaryTemplate below it). A path like ../../etc/passwd enables arbitrary file read (path traversal).

archiveVisitPacket joins the user-controlled packetLabel (from POST body in src/app/api/visit-summaries/[id]/packet/route.ts) directly into the file path without path.basename sanitization (unlike archiveLabelPrintout). A label such as ../../.../file allows arbitrary file write outside the packet directory.

retrieveExternalLabReport fetches an arbitrary reportUrl without validating the host (the imaging equivalent below validates against TRUSTED_IMAGING_HOSTS). The URL comes from the `lab-report-url` header in src/app/api/labs/inbound/route.ts, allowing SSRF against internal services or the local network.

queryEmployeeDirectory builds an LDAP filter `(cn=*${searchTerm}*)` by concatenating the unescaped user search term (from GET ?q in src/app/api/admin/staff-directory/route.ts). The escapeLdapValue helper exists but is not used here, allowing LDAP injection (e.g. injecting )(&(...)) to alter the query and enumerate arbitrary directory entries.

resolveLabelAttachmentHeaders places the user-controlled displayTitle (GET ?document_title in src/app/api/prescriptions/[id]/label/route.ts) directly into the Content-Disposition header without stripping CR/LF (unlike resolvePacketAttachmentHeaders which sanitizes). This allows HTTP header injection / response splitting.

The iron-session cookie secret falls back to a hardcoded default value when SESSION_SECRET is not set. Anyone who knows the default can forge valid session cookies (including clinic_admin sessions) and bypass authentication.

The draft encryption key is derived from a hardcoded fallback string when DRAFT_SIGNING_SECRET is not set, so encrypted clinician draft contents can be decrypted by anyone using the known default key.

issueLegacyLabFeedKey generates the lab feed API key using Math.random(), which is not cryptographically secure and is predictable. An attacker who observes one key can predict future feed keys and impersonate the lab feed.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator

extra.message: submitPreVisitIntakeForm logs the full intake payload (including insuranceId, date of birth, and possibly SSN for legacy plans) to the server console on validation failure. This exposes sensitive patient PHI in logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: openVisitSummaryFromEmailLink (and openVisitSummaryFromPortalLink) decodes a base64 JSON token with no signature/HMAC and no expiry check (for the email-link path) and returns the visit summary for any summaryId. The endpoint src/app/api/visit-summaries/email-link/route.ts requires no authentication, so any caller can forge a token `{"summaryId":"<id>"}` and enumerate every patient's visit summary (diagnosis, care instructions, PHI).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: This route has no requireAuth() or any authentication/authorization check. Any unauthenticated caller can set the x-kiosk-clinician-id header and modify any clinician's specialty in the database.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: resumeVendorSyncDestination returns the raw x-redirect-url header value unvalidated, and src/app/api/appointments/sync/route.ts uses it in NextResponse.redirect(new URL(destination, request.url)). An attacker can craft a URL that redirects a logged-in admin to a malicious external site.

formatScheduleSyncError returns the full error message and stack trace whenever the caller sets ?verbose=1 (a caller-controlled query parameter), leaking internal server details. formatEligibilityError similarly leaks stack traces in development.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: reopenRefillDraft decrypts AES-256-CBC without any authentication tag and distinguishes padding errors (returning a distinct 'corrupted/padding' error vs a generic error in src/app/api/prescriptions/[id]/refill-draft/route.ts). This is a padding-oracle / unauthenticated-cipher weakness that lets an attacker tamper with and recover encrypted draft contents.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: loadApplicationConfig merges the entire admin settings payload into the shared runtimeConfig object via Object.assign without any allowlist, permitting arbitrary keys (including __proto__) to be written into a globally-shared configuration object used by the reminder worker and waiting-room display.

cwe: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')

extra.message: saveLetterheadAsset joins the raw uploaded filename (file.name) directly into the branding directory path without sanitization. A crafted filename (e.g. ../../...) allows writing the uploaded file outside the intended public/branding directory.

When creating a patient, a missing password defaults to the hardcoded value "changeme123" (same in src/app/api/import/route.ts:129). Accounts created this way are protected by a predictable, publicly-known default password.
